problem: Prior natural-language navigation systems are shown in simulation or on large datasets, but are rarely deployed and rigorously tested on real robots in unknown real environments, and typically lack spoken dialogue with a real person.
motivation: Real deployment requires interpreting spoken instructions into an executable plan in buildings unseen a priori. Only the abstract was available, so further motivation details are not visible.
key_idea: A real-robot framework that uses spoken dialogue with a human to turn navigational instructions into a plan and then execute it in a novel, unknown indoor environment.
insight: Per the abstract, dialogue-based instruction interpretation outperforms three prior vision-and-language navigation methods when all are tested in the same real environments. No ablations or analysis are visible from the abstract alone.
method: Spoken dialogue interface: interacts with a real person to clarify and interpret navigational instructions into a plan (details not available, abstract only)
Plan execution: the robot executes the resulting plan in a novel indoor environment (details not available)
numbers_note: abstract only; the paper reports 39 trials across 3 test buildings but the abstract gives no metric values
results: Evaluated on a real robot in 39 trials across 3 novel test buildings, and reported to outperform three prior VLN methods in the same environment. No numeric values are available from the abstract.
limitations: Requires a human dialogue partner at test time
compares_to: three prior vision-and-language navigation methods (unnamed in abstract)
